Plate Curator on Vercel: results

Answer

Yes. About 6× sooner on a 100-plate batch, with the same tag quality, for about $2 more per full 8,325-plate pass.

The problem and the plan are in part 1⁠↗.

*Best of a separate 10-model Gateway run on the same 15 plates and prompt. Gemma 4 26B scored 0.647 in that run.

One score from 0 to 1 that balances precision (suggestions already in the catalog) and recall (catalog tags found). “Micro” pools every tag across the 15 plates before scoring, so each tag counts the same. It’s a standard score for multi-label tagging, where one plate gets several tags. Sources: Zhang and Zhou, IEEE TKDE 2014⁠↗; Sokolova and Lapalme, 2009⁠↗; scikit-learn metrics guide⁠↗.

With the same model on both routes, only where it runs changes.

Known limitations and risks

Proven on staging samples, not yet at catalog scale.

  • Editorial quality. 15 Alaska plates against existing labels; a broader reviewed sample is needed.
  • Stages moved as they are. Hosted runs use the team’s existing prompts and scripts; tuning them was out of scope, and every stage has room to improve.
  • Cost. Model charges only; Functions and Workflow usage aren’t in the estimate.
  • No rollback yet. Checks run before release; rollback is built before cutover. Cutover plan⁠↗
  • Research route undecided. Seven-plate retest only; next, an Eve agent works out the Wiki link, Describe and Story workflow.

Development tooling

I set the boundaries and architecture; agents built it under my review.

I used VS Code as my editor and Herdr⁠↗ as my main terminal workspace for Claude Code and Codex. I chose the migration boundaries, ran the first Firebase spike, read the Next.js and Vercel docs, and helped build the first components on Next.js primitives. Then I handed my target architecture to the agents, worked through the approach with them against current best practices, and approved it before they drove the build. I reviewed their changes and rehearsed the Editor and Owner flows in staging.

    Same plates and prompt, scored against catalog tags.
